title: Lesson 2: Lightning Tables 11-19 - Ekadhikena Pattern
learningGoals: Recognise the digit-sum pattern in the table of 11 and extend it to tables 12–19.
Apply the Ekadhikena sutra to build each table row by progressive addition.
Multiply any 2-digit number by 11 instantly, handling carry when the digit sum exceeds 9.
coreIdeas: Table of 11: place the digit, add digit+1 in the middle position — 11×23 = 2(2+3)3 = 253.
Tables 12–19 are built by adding the multiplier to the previous product — one more each time.
When the middle sum exceeds 9, carry 1 to the left digit — the same carry rule as normal addition.

workedExamples.method: Split 35: left digit 3, right digit 5, middle = 3+5 = 8. Write 3 | 8 | 5 = 385.
Split 47: left digit 4, right digit 7, middle = 4+7 = 11. Carry: (4+1)|1|7 = 517.
Table of 13: start from 13, add 13 each step. Row 7 = 91.

starterPractice: Write the table of 11 from 11×1 to 11×9 using the digit-sum pattern.
Use progressive addition to write the table of 14.
11 × 54 = ? (check: does the middle digit need a carry?)

onboarding.coachIntro: Today you will spot the pattern inside tables 11 to 19, so you can build the answers instead of memorising them one by one.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at group A. If the learner already knows table of 11 perfectly, jump to group C.

mission.missionPromise: Spot the pattern for 11 first, then climb through 12 to 19 with fast, steady number steps.
mission.successCelebration: Well done. You can now use the pattern to build products from tables 11 to 19 with confidence.

microLessonPattern: Coach reveals the pattern with one punchy demonstration.
Board shows the digit-sum rule with colour arrows.
Student reads the pattern aloud before practising.
Student builds the next row themselves before seeing the answer.
Instant feedback highlights the exact digit that was wrong.
Review prompt asks the student to explain the pattern in their own words.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 18 XP per exercise group based on difficulty.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak counter visible; a correct answer on retry still counts as streak-save.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group earns a themed badge tied to the table skill being practised.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short coach cheer, XP pulse animation, and progress bar moves forward.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two wrong answers in one group triggers a mini re-teach with a smaller multiplier.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Re-show the worked board step, then give a simpler multiplication to try.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the student answers the checkpoint correctly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Missed groups reappear at the start of the next session as warm-up cards.

uiDirectives.noScrollGoal: Student sees mission progress, question card, and action buttons without scrolling.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Build the table of 11
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let us start with one number that feels magical. In the table of 11, the outside digits stay in place, and their sum slips into the middle.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show 11 x 23 as 2 _ 3. Add 2 + 3 = 5, so the answer becomes 253. Then show 11 x 34 as 3 _ 4 and fill 7 in the middle to make 374.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Say the rule with me: outside digits stay, middle is their sum. Now what is 11 x 23?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: build 11 x 41 by keeping 4 and 1 outside and filling the middle.
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: What is 11 x 52 when you use the same pattern?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes. You kept the outside digits and built the middle correctly.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Keep 4 and 1 outside first. Then add 4 + 1 = 5 and place it in the middle. That gives 451.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick pattern check: 11 x 13, 11 x 22, and 11 x 31.

exercises.hint: Keep outer digits 2 and 3. Put their sum (2+3=5) in the middle.

sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Start from 12×6=72 and add 12 more: 72+12=84. That is 12×7.

sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect carry! You handled the extra digit without any fuss.

screenplay.teacherLine: Watch me: 23 × 11. Keep the outer digits — 2 on the left, 3 on the right. Middle = 2+3 = 5. So the answer is 2 | 5 | 3 = 253. Simple!
screenplay.boardAction: Write 23 × 11. Draw blank: 2 _ 3. Reveal sum 2+3=5. Fill in 253. Box the answer.
screenplay.fallbackHint: Outer digits stay. Their sum goes in the middle.

screenplay.teacherLine: Your turn — let us do it together! 34 × 11. Outer digits: 3 and 4. What goes in the middle? 3+4 = ?
screenplay.boardAction: Write 34 × 11. Draw blank: 3 _ 4. Wait for student. Reveal 7. Write 374.
screenplay.fallbackHint: Add 3 + 4 to get the middle digit.

screenplay.teacherLine: When 4+7=11, the middle digit is 1 and we carry 1 to the left. So 4 becomes 5. Answer: 517!
screenplay.boardAction: Show 11×47 with carry arrow: 4+7=11, middle=1, left 4+1=5. Write 517.

visual.title: Eleven Trick with carry
visual.caption: If the middle sum is 10 or more, carry 1 to the left digit.

screenplay.teacherLine: Watch the carry. 11 × 47: digit sum = 4+7 = 11. Middle digit = 1 (units of 11). Carry 1 to the left: 4+1 = 5. Answer: 517. The carry is just like normal addition!
screenplay.boardAction: Show 11×47: write 4+7=11. Arrow to middle → 1. Carry arrow to left 4 → 5. Write 517.
screenplay.fallbackHint: Middle = units digit of the sum. Carry 1 to the left.
